headline: Why millets suit dryland farming
caption:
Why millets suit dryland farming

Millets can grow on arid lands with minimal inputs and are resilient to changes in climate.

Why it matters: this is a millet-specific fact worth understanding.

Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) (2022-12-06)

headline: Meet India's diverse millet family
caption:
Meet India's diverse millet family

Sorghum, pearl millet, finger millet, foxtail millet, little millet, kodo millet, barnyard millet and proso millet are distinct millet crops.

Why it matters: this is a millet-specific fact worth understanding.

Source: ICAR–Indian Institute of Millets Research (2023-01-01)

headline: Millets carry centuries of food heritage
caption:
Millets carry centuries of food heritage

Millets are among the first plants to be domesticated and have served as a traditional staple crop for millions of farmers in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia.

Why it matters: this is a millet-specific fact worth understanding.

Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) (2023-01-01)
